author: Matthew Neschis
title: Bill Belichick and North Carolina break silence amid buyout talks and disastrous start - NewsBreak
text:
By Matthew Neschis ,
33 minutes ago Bill Belichick reaffirmed his commitment to North Carolina on Wednesday By Getty Images Bill Belichick reaffirmed his commitment to North Carolina as rumors continue to swirl that the Tar Heels head coach has already discussed potential exit strategies .
Belichick’s tenure thus far in Chapel Hill has been nothing short of a disaster, with scandals and sloppy play rearing their ugly heads on a daily basis.
In the latest off-field headache for the NFL legend, cornerbacks coach Armond Hawkins was slapped with a suspension for breaking NCAA regulations .
The Tar Heels haven’t exactly eased tensions with their production on the gridiron, as North Carolina boasts a meagre 2-3 record while losing a combined 120-33 to Power Four opponents.

Despite the rocky start to Belichick’s time at North Carolina, both sides asserted that they were willing to see this experiment out.
"I'm fully committed to UNC Football and the program we're building here," Belichick said in an official statement posted to X on Wednesday.
North Carolina director of athletics Bubba Cunningham returned the favor, adding: "Coach Belichick has the full support of the Department of Athletics and University."
Though Belichick and Cunningham publicly voiced their desire to stick together, recent rumblings tell a different story.
According to 247 Sports, North Carolina held "preliminary conversations" about firing Belichick — a costly decision that would force the university to pay off the $20 million buyout outlined in his contract.
It appears as though Belichick is at the very least entertaining the idea, with journalist Ollie Connolly reporting that he has "discussed buyout options with North Carolina’s hierarchy.”
During these conversations, Belichick has "signaled a willingness to trigger his own $1 million buyout if he can find a soft landing with another team or in media."
In order to get ahead of Belichick’s potentially impending departure, members of his coaching staff have allegedly been in contact with other programs that will likely be competing in the College Football Playoff in hopes of assuming roles during the postseason.
In North Carolina’s last game — a 38-10 loss to Clemson — Belichick’s squad fell behind 28-3 by the end of the first quarter en route to entering halftime down 32 points.
Over the last two weeks, members of UNC’s coaching staff told Connolly that Belichick has come off as “weird” and “distant” while communicating with his colleagues. During the Tar Heels’ bye week, several coaches conceded that they couldn’t even get him on the phone.
